notes.text: The sheet is manuscript text in his hand, with author number 2), a diagonal left-margin note, two mathematical diagram blocks, numerous revisions, and thin lower-left foliation 13 in another or undetermined hand. The entire original and both supplied native halves were read once; all fifteen saved crops were inspected once. P10 is rotated 45 degrees clockwise for reading, while every recorded coordinate remains in the original 1685 by 2363 image. The main text has nineteen physical prose lines, one equality display and one triangular diagram block (line_count 21 by this convention); the diagonal margin is inventoried separately. H’s foliation discussion, note about its added vertical arrow and proposed famille correction are editorial, not manuscript text.

Targeted boundary check. The source says “Mais on ne peut pas dire … en général que dot T soit la frontière de T dans X” and gives X=T with dot T not equal to the written 0. For any space X, the topological boundary of X inside itself is closure_X(X) minus interior_X(X), hence empty. Taking a nonempty Y and X=T=Y×[0,1], with the distinguished outer section dot T=Y×{1}, gives a nonempty dot T and empty ambient frontier. Thus the displayed counterexample mechanism is valid. This checks that mechanism only: reference (7) is read from its ink and the unavailable earlier statement numbered (7) is not reconstructed. The source’s un-crossed oval 0 is retained, not silently changed to phi or an empty-set glyph.

Independent local re-proof of the collar/mapping-cylinder equivalence, conditional on cônique having its usual mapping-cylinder meaning here. Let f:B→Y be a homeomorphism and let C(f) be the quotient of Y disjoint union (B×[0,1]) by (b,0) identified with f(b). The map sending the base y to (y,0) and the class of (b,r) to (f(b),r) is well-defined and continuous by the quotient property. Its inverse sends (y,r) to the class of (f^{-1}(y),r); this is continuous and agrees with the base identification at r=0. The two maps compose to the identities, so C(f)≃Y×[0,1] and the base inclusion becomes y↦(y,0), precisely the commutativity of diagram (10). Conversely a product collar transports the identity-map cone structure on Y×[0,1]. This proof uses an explicitly stated interpretation of the cone construction; the assigned leaf does not define all of its earlier notation. No extra bar on T is justified by this interpretation.

Targeted check of the absolute-cone and strip examples. Under the standard radial convention, away from the cone vertex the absolute cone on B has the product coordinates B×(0,1]. For any 0<a<1, the strip B×[a,1] is a collar neighborhood of the outer section B×{1}; the coordinate u=(1-r)/(1-a) sends that section to u=0 and gives B×[0,1]. For a positive radius lambda, the same construction on [a lambda,lambda] collars the section B×{lambda} inside the truncated cone T_lambda. This requires lambda>0; the source’s line does not state its range anew, and no assertion about the vertex radius zero is inferred. For a product strip B×[a,b] with a<b, each endpoint section has a collar obtained by a sufficiently short endpoint subinterval. Their union has a collar by choosing two disjoint endpoint subintervals and taking the disjoint union of those product collars. Therefore the three listed boundary choices are valid if the live barred-E-p operator denotes that radial strip and 0<epsilon<1. The operator is not defined on this leaf, so that identification and parameter range remain explicit hypotheses, not purported recovered definitions. The first epsilon/delta/lambda reading remains unresolved despite the expected strip formula.

Refined statement `150_scan014.N05.H`: Independent re-proof of the closing finite-union statement under the compact-Hausdorff convention, and assuming the uncertain lower J/I denotes the same finite index set as the preceding family. Let Y_i be finitely many pairwise disjoint closed subsets of compact Hausdorff X, and write Y for their union. Each Y_i is clopen in Y. If h:Y×[0,1]→T is a collar with h(y,0)=y and T a neighborhood of Y, then h(Y_i×[0,1]) is a neighborhood of Y_i: its product component is open in T, and intersecting it with an ambient open neighborhood of Y contained in T gives an ambient open neighborhood of Y_i. The restricted h is its collar. Conversely choose pairwise disjoint ambient open neighborhoods U_i of the Y_i, using normality for a finite family. For a collar h_i:Y_i×[0,1]→T_i, the preimage of U_i∩T_i is open and contains the compact zero section Y_i×{0}. A finite subcover by product neighborhoods provides delta_i>0 such that h_i(Y_i×[0,delta_i]) lies in U_i. Each shortened strip is still a neighborhood of Y_i: the smaller relatively open product Y_i×[0,delta_i) intersects an ambient neighborhood contained in T_i. Rescaling each shortened interval and taking the finite disjoint union gives a bijective collar Y×[0,1]→the union of those strips. Continuity follows from the finite clopen decomposition of Y, and its inverse follows either piecewise from the disjoint U_i or from compactness of the domain and Hausdorffness of X. This proves both directions under the stated separation and indexing hypotheses. The source’s “une partie finie” is retained; it can mean a finite collection here and is not changed to H’s proposed famille.

Counterexample to the weaker quasi-compact variant of N05, without a Hausdorff convention or an additional requirement that each collar neighborhood be closed in X. Form X from two copies of [0,1] by identifying equal t>0 and keeping their origins o_1,o_2 distinct. It is quasi-compact as a quotient of a finite disjoint union of compact intervals. Each {o_i} is closed. The subset U_i={o_i} union (0,1] is open in X and is homeomorphic to [0,1], so it is a product collar of its origin. The pair Y={o_1,o_2} is closed and discrete as a subspace. It has no collar: if Y×[0,1] embedded as a neighborhood T with the prescribed zero section, its two clopen product components, intersected with an ambient open neighborhood of Y contained in T, would give disjoint ambient open neighborhoods of the two origins. Every neighborhood of either origin contains a positive initial interval, so any two such neighborhoods intersect. This is a contradiction. The example refutes only that weakened interpretation of compact; it does not refute the manuscript statement under the customary compact-Hausdorff convention. If another page imposes closed collar neighborhoods or a separated-space convention, this particular example does not satisfy those strengthened hypotheses. No other page was consulted.

Targeted typing diagnostic for the diagonal marginal map. The upper target is literally [0,1], while the lower rule is y↦(y,0). For a general topological space Y, the pair (y,0) is an element of Y×[0,1], not of [0,1]. Thus the written two-row map has a type mismatch unless an unstated special identification is imposed. The natural repaired target would be Y×[0,1], consistent with the preceding product isomorphism, but that repair is not put into the transcription. The upper connector itself has no secure head, so its direction is also left doubtful.

The final lower index is J-shaped and is retained as J|I doubt beside the earlier clear I. If it is literally J and differs from I, the collection being unioned is not specified by the preceding clause, so N05 is a proof only for the intended same-index formulation, not a validation of an undefined J. Ink alone does not decide whether this is an authorial slip, a compressed I, or an unprovided convention. The operator bar(E)p_epsilon(T) has a true additional overbar above E only, a separate p and baseline (T); its interpretation is not used to remove the source’s separate first epsilon/delta/lambda ambiguity.

Revision and punctuation diagnostics. The isolated raised É/E is not expanded to Évitons, and the slanted word structure is transcribed only in the margin where it is written. The two Y variables visibly overwrite earlier Z forms; both layers are preserved. The heavy initial cylindrique group does not yield an independently readable additional cancelled word. Both main homéom forms have no stop, but the marginal homéom. has a real dot. The source writes cônique twice. Root audit identifies the isolated irregular blot below faux as lacking a recoverable linguistic or geometric structure; the draft graphic is removed and its crop remains available. The final le sont, with sont now explicitly uncertain, reaches the paper edge without a recoverable following full stop. A curved insertion leader at (absolu) and one at en général are attachment strokes, not extra parentheses/underlines. These are source-state decisions, not mathematical emendations.

Independent root audit personally inspected all 16 nonidentical crops, including the isolated blot and the complete triangle/marginal map, and a wider native-image opening. Five boxes were revised. First/second readings and their hashes remain fixed; final adjudications record the exclusion of the nonsemantic blot separately from actual source changes.

Constructed mutually inverse continuous maps for the mapping cylinder of a homeomorphism and the product collar; converse by transport of structure, under the stated interpretation of cônique.
Constructed endpoint collar coordinates and disjoint endpoint substrips; checked only positive radii/nondegenerate strips and explicitly conditional interpretation of the undefined strip operator.
Proved the finite disjoint closed-union collar equivalence in compact Hausdorff X with a common finite index set; used normality and compactness/tube shrinking explicitly.

Refuted N05.Q, the weakened quasi-compact/non-Hausdorff version with collars merely neighborhoods, by the compact interval with two origins. This does not refute N05.H, the compact-Hausdorff same-index version proved in N05, nor a separately imposed closed-collar formulation.
Checked the types: y↦(y,0) naturally lands in Y×[0,1], while the manuscript target is [0,1]. Retained the written target and the connector uncertainty.
Separated the literal unresolved J/I index from the same-index hypothesis needed for the finite-union proof; no formula was silently regularized.
